clue.text: Boxes with drug in limited supply

blocks.note: to spar is to box, so boxes as a verb is spars
E is short for ecstasy, the standard crossword drug

explanation.surface: A boxer finds the performance-enhancing drugs he wants are hard to come by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like containers but is the verb: a boxer spars.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sparse is thinly scattered or scanty, the adjective for a meagre supply.

clue.text: In drastic way, cut off cathedral city

blocks.note: to sever is to cut off
Ely is the small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A cathedral city has been drastically isolated, cut off from the outside world.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely is an adverb meaning harshly or seriously, which is acting in a drastic manner.

clue.text: A dispute about right way to show direction

indicators.note: about means going around, so the dispute wraps the abbreviation for right

blocks.note: taken as written
a row is a quarrel or dispute
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over the correct route to signpost.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a symbol drawn on signs to point the way, a means of indicating direction.

clue.text: Be angry about pound as one wanting rid of corporation?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for being angry wraps the unit

blocks.note: to simmer is to seethe with suppressed anger
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone fumes over money, as if wanting to abolish a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old jocular word for a large belly, not a business, so the one wanting rid of it is a dieter.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimmer is a person on a diet trying to lose weight, here a paunch humorously called a corporation.

clue.text: Inclined to stress part of capital I control

indicators.note: part of says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of capital, the I, and the start of control

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of a capital letter I tilts it for emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right and is used in print to emphasise words.

clue.text: Piece of canvas pretty serious artist initially used in work

indicators.note: initially means taking just the opening letter of each of the three words before it
used in means placed inside, so those letters go into the word for labour

blocks.note: toil is hard work
the first letters of pretty, serious and artist

explanation.surface: A rather earnest painter starts using a canvas in a new work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' suggests a painting, but it is sailcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest one on a mast, and sails are made of canvas.

clue.text: Person who washes, so to speak, linen garment

indicators.note: so to speak says the next word is to be taken by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: lawn is a fine linen fabric; its sound is spelt differently here
a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: Someone who does the washing, as it were, handles linen and garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawn is a fine sheer linen or cotton cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman whose job is washing and ironing clothes.

clue.text: Revealing intelligence Conservative Party turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: Intelligence leaks out as Conservative Party members show up.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever describes someone or something showing quick intelligence and skill.

clue.text: Survey completed, that is put in car

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the abbreviation goes within the vehicle

blocks.note: something over is finished or completed
VW, a Volkswagen, is a car
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A finished questionnaire is placed in someone's car.
explanation.definitionFit: An overview is a general survey or summary of a subject.

clue.text: Warm clothing in Washington area in bad weather

indicators.note: bad means spoiled or not right, so the letters before and after are reworked

blocks.note: Washington lies in DC, the District of Columbia
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People in Washington wrap up warm when the weather turns foul.
explanation.walkthrough: All three pieces are shuffled together; 'in' looks like a placement word but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A windcheater is a windproof jacket, a garment that keeps the wearer warm.

clue.text: Trapping you orally in section of exam? Poor fellow

indicators.note: orally means spoken, so the word is replaced by the letter that sounds like it
trapping means holding within, so the exam section wraps the sound

blocks.note: an exam is often sat as several papers
the letter U is pronounced like you

explanation.surface: An oral exam question catches a candidate out, leaving the poor fellow floundering.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper is a very poor person, someone with no means at all.

clue.text: Was in no-win situation, so pulled out

blocks.note: first meaning: finished a game level, with no winner
second meaning: extracted, as a gun from a holster

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a hopeless position withdrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled out' suggests withdrawing, but it is drawing out a weapon or a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Drew is the past tense of draw, both to tie a match and to extract something.

clue.text: Angry about new name being disrespectfully treated

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for angry goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: mad means angry
N is the abbreviation for new
a handle is slang for a name or nickname

explanation.surface: Someone is furious that their new name is being treated with contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle is to push someone around roughly, treating them without respect.

clue.text: Male equivalent of shocking pink?

blocks.note: surface reading: what colour a man would wear instead of a garish pink
setter's reading: boys are traditionally dressed in blue where girls get pink, and shocking becomes the electrical sense, a vivid shade with a jolt

explanation.walkthrough: Shocking pink is a vivid magenta; swap the girls' colour for the boys' and 'shocking' for its electrical twin.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric blue is a brilliant, steely bright blue, as vivid among blues as shocking pink is among pinks.

clue.text: Card one dramatically played

blocks.note: first meaning: an eccentric or amusing person
second meaning: a role taken by an actor in a play

explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' tempts toward playing cards to go with 'played', but it means a comical eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Character can mean an odd, colourful person, or a figure portrayed in a drama.

clue.text: Dislike one particular edition of book

blocks.note: a means one
a version is a particular form or edition of a text

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes one specific edition of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong feeling of distaste for something, the noun for dislike.

clue.text: Even I, perhaps, could become so fearful

indicators.note: could become suggests the letters turning into something else by being rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, all twelve letters

explanation.surface: A speaker admits that even they might end up scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehensive means anxious that something bad may happen, a synonym of afraid.

clue.text: Lady in crowd surrounding East European

indicators.note: surrounding means going around, so the crowd wraps the two abbreviations

blocks.note: a press is a dense crowd of people
E is the abbreviation for East
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A noblewoman stands in a throng gathered round an Eastern European.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress is a woman holding a peerage, entitled to be called Lady.

clue.text: Outshine learner in convoluted pieces

indicators.note: convoluted means twisted and tangled, so the letters are rearranged
in means placed inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: taken as written
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner shines in an intricate set of pieces of music.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse someone is to surpass them so they are overshadowed, which is to outshine.

clue.text: Stop and take a breather after a run

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
to rest is to take a breather

explanation.surface: A jogger stops to catch their breath after going for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the breather after the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt its progress, a formal synonym of stop.

clue.text: Not of practical use? Old man learnt differently

indicators.note: differently means in another way, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old man learnt things differently, none of it practical.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a decoration is defined by what it is not: useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornamental serves as decoration rather than having a practical function.

clue.text: Amount of wood that's cut after delivery

blocks.note: first meaning: a measure of cut firewood, 128 cubic feet
second meaning: the umbilical link snipped after a baby is born

explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a timber load arriving, but it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord is both a stacked unit of firewood and the umbilical tie severed at birth.

clue.text: Copper section, in length between foot and yard

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a piece or section

explanation.surface: A section of copper pipe measures somewhere between a foot and a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient measure of the forearm, about eighteen inches, longer than a foot and shorter than a yard.

clue.text: Recent changes giving us heart

indicators.note: changes means alterations, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Latest developments have given everyone fresh encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its middle or core, which is its centre.

clue.text: Something religious left outside tavern in US, for instance

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the first piece wraps the drinking place

blocks.note: a relic is a sacred object left behind by a saint
a pub is a tavern

explanation.surface: A religious tract is left outside an American bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the abbreviation L, but it belongs to the description of a relic.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is an example of a republic, a state with an elected head rather than a monarch.

clue.text: Refuse to include husband in party

indicators.note: to include means taking something inside, so the rubbish word holds the abbreviation

blocks.note: trash is refuse or rubbish
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone declines to invite their husband to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb decline, but it is the noun rubbish. A thrash is informal British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a thrash is a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Worker in church holding cross in attack

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the attack phrase wraps the symbol

blocks.note: to set on someone is to attack them
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A church employee carries a cross while under attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building and graveyard.
